name: TensorRT-LLM: Llama 3.1 8B FP8 on 1x H100 SXM 80GB, ISL/OSL 1000/1000
methodology: Engine: TensorRT-LLM PyTorch backend (v0.19+ workflow, no engine build), trtllm-bench throughput. Hardware: 1x NVIDIA H100 SXM 80GB (DGX H100). Tensor-parallel size = 1 (single GPU), pipeline parallel 1. Prompt length ISL = 1000, output length OSL = 1000, uniform (input/output stdev 0) from a synthetic token-norm-dist dataset of 3000 requests. Concurrency: NOT stated and NOT fixed - this is an offline max-load scenario where all requests are queued back to back, so effective concurrency is whatever the scheduler sustains; the source omits the achieved batch size / request count in flight. Figure is AGGREGATE output tokens/s for the single GPU (trtllm-bench 'Total Output Throughput'), not per-request and not per-user. KV cache free-memory fraction 0.95. CUDA graphs enabled with padding across batch sizes 1-8192.
notes: Measured by NVIDIA, published in the TensorRT-LLM performance overview and reproducible with the documented `prepare_dataset.py` + `trtllm-bench throughput --backend pytorch` workflow (llm_options.yml with CUDA-graph batch sizes 1..8192, kv_cache_free_gpu_mem_fraction 0.95). Metric is 'Total Output Throughput (tokens/sec)' as trtllm-bench reports it: AGGREGATE output tokens/s across all in-flight requests at the stated TP size, under an offline infinite-rate request feed, NOT per-request and NOT per-GPU. Model weights are NVIDIA-published ModelOpt-quantized checkpoints. The page explicitly states these are reference points, not peak performance, and that batch size / parallelism were left mostly at defaults.
